Arizona Financial Theatre Parking Guide: Seating, Drop-Off and Upcoming Shows

Scottsdale Sprinters’ short answer on Arizona Financial Theatre parking: the venue’s garage is the Adams Street Garage at 4th Avenue and Adams Street, which typically opens at 6 p.m. on weekdays and earlier on weekends and takes no cash. The theatre is at 400 West Washington Street in downtown Phoenix, doors generally open an hour before the show, and a guest being dropped off is sent to 4th Avenue and Adams Street, near the main entrance. For a group, one chauffeured vehicle replaces the garage, the card reader and the drive home.

Last updated: September 26, 2026

Prices start at $125 an hour for the Luxury SUV (Suburban), which seats 6, on a 4-hour minimum, so the shortest booking is $500 before 8% tax. Every vehicle is booked by the hour at its published rate and minimum, with no per-seat pricing.

How does parking work at Arizona Financial Theatre?

Arizona Financial Theatre’s parking is the Adams Street Garage at 4th Avenue and Adams Street, next to the venue: it typically opens at 6 p.m. Monday to Friday and earlier on weekends, spaces are sold online, at the box office or at the garage entrance on show days, and the garage is cashless. The venue says the 6 p.m. weekday opening does not apply to weekday shows that start before 6 p.m. There are accessible parking spaces on every level of the garage, with elevator access. The venue’s pages publish no parking price: spaces are sold per show. Pay by card or phone, and buy the space ahead when the garage matters to your group. Every point of sale inside the venue is cashless too, credit, debit or mobile pay, with cash-to-card conversion at the upgrade podium.

Where is the drop-off at Arizona Financial Theatre?

If you are being dropped off at Arizona Financial Theatre, tell staff as you arrive and they direct you to 4th Avenue and Adams Street, near the main entrance; that corner, beside the Adams Street Garage where most cars park, is the one drop-off point the venue publishes for guests arriving by car. That is the point a chauffeured group uses too. We tell staff we are dropping off, unload the group where they direct at 4th Avenue and Adams Street, and agree one pickup point for the ride home before the show. The venue publishes no separate area for rideshare, limousines or charters, so no curb is held for booked vehicles. If the venue posts a drop-off plan for a show, that plan comes first. A group that splits across cars also splits across the garage, the card readers and the exit line. One vehicle arrives with everyone at once and leaves with everyone at once.

Where is Arizona Financial Theatre, and how do you get there?

Arizona Financial Theatre is at 400 West Washington Street, Phoenix, AZ 85003, in downtown Phoenix within 1 mile of the Phoenix Convention Center; the box office and will call sit in front of the building on the corner of 4th Avenue and Washington Street, and the venue’s garage is next to it at 4th Avenue and Adams Street. Live Nation runs the venue. By car, set the navigation to the garage at 4th Avenue and Adams Street rather than the street address, so the last turn is the garage entrance, not the front of the building. A chauffeured group needs neither: the driver takes the group to the drop-off at 4th Avenue and Adams Street and waits for the ride home.

What time do doors open at Arizona Financial Theatre?

Doors at Arizona Financial Theatre generally open 1 hour before the show’s scheduled start time unless the show says otherwise, and your ticket has the exact time; the venue recommends arriving early, and every show is mobile entry, with tickets on your phone rather than printed or emailed. The box office opens on show days only, typically at 5 p.m., and 90 minutes before show time for a morning or afternoon show. It handles will call with a picture ID that matches the name on the order and the confirmation number, at (602) 379-2800. VIP and Meet & Greet check-in can begin before the garage or the doors open, and its instructions come from the official VIP provider, typically 24 to 72 hours before the show. Camping out overnight is not permitted. All events are all ages unless the show says otherwise, and every child over one year old needs a ticket.

What is the Arizona Financial Theatre bag policy?

Bags up to 12 by 6 by 12 inches are allowed inside Arizona Financial Theatre, every bag is searched before entry, bags that are not clear get an additional search, and no backpacks are allowed; each guest may bring up to 2 factory-sealed water bottles of up to 1 liter, but no Hydroflasks. Not allowed: outside food or drinks, unsealed liquids or gels, personal video cameras and GoPros, selfie sticks, drones, masks, laser pointers, glowsticks and K-Pop light sticks, stuffed animals and toys, and weapons of any kind. The venue says the list can change by show. Arizona Financial Theatre is a non-smoking building, with designated smoking areas outside depending on the event. Settle bags at the hotel: a group that is dropped off has no car in the garage to go back to during the show.

What is the seating like at Arizona Financial Theatre, and how many people does it hold?

Arizona Financial Theatre is a multi-level theatre that Live Nation’s special events team lists at up to 5,000 guests for a full-venue event, with a pit area on the floor, a club level, and VIP Suites above the club level, each with theatre-style seats and a small lounge, the suite level with its own private bar. The layout changes with the show: the venue’s floor plans set the room for concert seating, concert seating with an orchestra, Broadway seating and boxing. Some shows are reserved seating, where you see your seat when you pick the ticket, and some are general admission. Movable walls and padded chairs let the venue size the room to the show, and a 1,700 square foot VIP lounge sits beside the wrap-around lobby. For a group, the seating decides the arrival: a general admission night rewards getting in together at doors, and on a reserved night everyone already has a seat.

Which vehicle fits an Arizona Financial Theatre group?

A VIP night takes the Maybach Jet Sprinter, the Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter, the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter or the Luxury SUV (Suburban). Friends and birthday crews ride the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax), the Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) or the Party Bus (28 Pax). Company nights and big groups take the Executive Black Sprinter, the Executive White Sprinter, the Mini Bus (24 Pax) or the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax). Seat counts are seated capacities from the fleet: the Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter seats 15, the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) 13, the Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) 16, the Party Bus (28 Pax) 28 and the Maybach Jet Sprinter 9. The Executive Black Sprinter seats 14, the Mini Bus (24 Pax) 24 and the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) 29. Our pick for a show night downtown is the Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter, $250 an hour with a 4-hour minimum: fiber-optic lighting with eighteen modes, an ultra-premium sound system and a full partition with an intercom to your chauffeur. The Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) is $175 an hour with a 4-hour minimum, and the Executive Black Sprinter is $145 an hour with a 4-hour minimum. Every rate prices the whole vehicle, before tax. Count riders for the ride home as well as the ride there; the late list is the one that matters. For a group bigger than one vehicle, we plan two or more and quote them together.

How should a group plan the ride to an Arizona Financial Theatre show?

Plan backwards from the show time on the ticket: doors generally open 1 hour before it, so a pickup that lands the group at the 4th Avenue and Adams Street drop-off around doors leaves room for the bag search, the mobile tickets and, on a general admission night, getting in together. The ride home is the part to plan hardest. Agree the pickup point before the show, and your chauffeur is there when the house lights come up, so the group walks out to its own vehicle instead of the garage line. Events are all ages unless the show says otherwise. If even one passenger is under 21, the trip is alcohol-free for the whole group, adults included; we sell no alcohol on any trip. Book by the hour and the vehicle is yours for the whole night, dinner downtown before the show included, or book a ride there and a ride back. Reach the reservations team at (623) 986-6339 or reservations@scottsdalesprinters.com with the show, the date, the pickup area and the rider count.

Frequently asked questions

Where do you park for Arizona Financial Theatre?

In the Adams Street Garage at 4th Avenue and Adams Street, next to the venue. It typically opens at 6 p.m. on weekdays and earlier on weekends, sells spaces online, at the box office or at the garage entrance on show days, and is cashless.

How much is parking at Arizona Financial Theatre?

The venue’s pages publish no price: spaces in the Adams Street Garage are sold per show, online, at the box office or at the garage entrance, and the garage takes no cash.

Where is the drop-off for Arizona Financial Theatre?

Tell staff you are being dropped off and they direct you to 4th Avenue and Adams Street, near the main entrance. A limo or party bus unloads there too, where staff direct.

What is the bag policy at Arizona Financial Theatre?

Bags up to 12 by 6 by 12 inches, searched at entry, with an additional search for bags that are not clear. No backpacks. Up to two factory-sealed water bottles of up to 1 liter per person; no Hydroflasks.

What time do doors open at Arizona Financial Theatre?

Generally one hour before the show’s scheduled start, unless the show says otherwise. The ticket has the exact time.

How many people does Arizona Financial Theatre hold?

Live Nation’s special events team lists the full venue at 5,000 guests. A show’s capacity depends on its layout: concert, orchestra, Broadway or boxing seating, reserved or general admission.

Is Arizona Financial Theatre seating reserved or general admission?

It depends on the show. On a reserved seated show you see your seat location when you pick the ticket; other shows are general admission. The venue has a pit area on the floor, a club level and VIP Suites above the club level.

Where is the box office at Arizona Financial Theatre?

On the corner of 4th Avenue and Washington Street, in front of the building. It opens on show days only, typically at 5 p.m., or 90 minutes before a morning or afternoon show.

Is Arizona Financial Theatre all ages?

Yes, unless the show says otherwise. Every child over one year old needs a ticket.

Is Arizona Financial Theatre cashless?

Yes. The garage and every point of sale take credit, debit or mobile pay; cash can be converted to a card at the upgrade podium.
